sentence: This project builds a delivery system made of fatty bubbles that fuse with cell membranes to place proteins and lipids into living cells.
This project provides microscopy and imaging tools that help researchers see changes in tissues and cells after exposure to environmental toxicants.
This project studies how a cancer gene changes tumor metabolism so that T cells stop working and the tumor escapes the immune system.
This project collects and studies MRI scans of the brain to understand brain changes linked to aging and disease.
This project builds an endoscope that uses light scattering to show how far colorectal cancer has grown into the colon wall.
This project studies how a gene called ZEB1 affects the risk of coronary artery disease in smooth muscle cells of blood vessels.
This project develops a treatment for breast cancer that spreads, using nanoparticles to carry a small RNA and a drug into the tumor.
This project builds mouse models of a rare brain tumor and tests whether the mice show epilepsy and early puberty.
This project uses mouse tumor models to find out how two oxygen-sensing proteins in tumor cells weaken the T cell response against cancer.
This project manages data and provides statistical support for studies that aim to cure chronic hepatitis B virus infection in people with HIV.
This project tries to find targets on T cells that recognize a thyroid cancer and to test whether they trigger immune responses.
This project studies how gene changes in blood cells of healthy people lead to leukemia.
This project uses embryonic stem cells from chickens to build genetic tools for making transgenic birds to study human diseases.
This project studies how the mouse brain processes color and joins it with the shape of what the animal sees.
This project tries to find out how fusion proteins keep cancer genes switched on in a type of leukemia and how those genes are silenced.
This project studies how Zika virus infects the heart of newborn mice and causes heart injury and failure.
This project runs a course that teaches hands-on proteomics methods and data analysis.
This project studies how small molecules called metabolites bind to proteins in order to learn what the metabolites do in cells.
This project develops tiny polymer drugs that cross the blood-brain barrier to treat a common type of brain cancer by acting on the tumor surroundings.
This project uses spatial transcriptomics to study kidney tissue from children with lupus nephritis and to understand the immune causes of the disease.
